issues.legal_issue: A government direction allowing seasonal cultivation of government land and giving adjacent landholders priority does not create a perpetual property right in their favour.
material_facts: The land belonged to the government and was exposed for cultivation only when water levels receded seasonally.
An earlier government resolution directed that the land be made available for cultivation to holders of adjoining survey numbers when feasible.
A later government memorandum superseded prior orders on disposal of the relevant lands and established a different priority policy.

The High Court accepted the adjoining landholders’ claim that the earlier resolution gave them a continuing right to cultivate the land, and the government’s later grant of a lease to a cooperative society was challenged on that basis.
issues.conclusion: The earlier resolution created no vested property right in the adjoining landholders; the High Court’s judgment was set aside, and the government remained free to grant leases under the policy it chose to adopt.
issues.legal_principle: A government policy or administrative direction concerning disposal of state property does not, without more, create an indefeasible property interest in prospective beneficiaries. The government may alter its policy, and a later policy may supersede an earlier one. Section 68 of the Bombay Land Revenue Code could not convert temporary, seasonal permission to cultivate government land into a permanent estate or tenure. The Court also regarded the later policy favouring local landless backward-class cooperative societies as consistent with the Directive Principles in Part IV of the Constitution. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: government_land_lease_appeal and land_remained_state_owned and seasonal_permission_only and (earlier_direction_favoured_adjacent_cultivators or later_policy_superseded_earlier_direction)

predicates.government_land_lease_appeal: A court is hearing an appeal concerning a government grant or lease of land that is claimed by reference to an administrative policy.
predicates.land_remained_state_owned: The land continued to belong to the government.
predicates.seasonal_permission_only: The government direction allowed cultivation only temporarily or seasonally, rather than granting a permanent tenure.
predicates.earlier_direction_favoured_adjacent_cult: An earlier government direction gave adjoining landholders priority or preference to cultivate the land.
predicates.later_policy_superseded_earlier_directio: The government later adopted a policy that superseded the earlier direction.

issues.definition: When a government-land lease appeal involves state-owned land and only seasonal permission, an earlier preference for adjacent cultivators, even if later superseded, does not sustain a claim to perpetual property rights.
